01 · The idea

AI makes it fast. It also makes it easy to copy.

A brand reel used to need a music licence, a photographer and a voice actor. Now one person makes it in an afternoon, with a trending sound, a photo from a search and a cloned voice. Each of those three can turn into a claim against you or against the brand.

The reel is built like a case file: one block per risk, and in each one the number is the hero (931 posts, $30,000, $150,000), so the risk is clear with the sound off. A small checklist fills 0/3 → 3/3 as each risk gets its fix.

02 · The checklist

The SAFE check, ready to copy.

This is what you asked for in the comments. Paste it into your project template and tick it on every reel before it goes up.

safe check · checklist
THE SAFE CHECK · run it on every reel before it goes up

1 · MUSIC
[ ] No trending / general-library sound on a brand account or a paid ad.
[ ] The track comes from the platform's commercial library (TikTok "Commercial Sounds",
    Meta "Sound Collection"), a stock library with a commercial licence, or it is original.
[ ] The licence (or the receipt) is saved with the project.

2 · IMAGES
[ ] No photo, illustration or logo pulled from a Google search.
[ ] Every image is ours, licensed stock (licence saved), or generated with a tool whose
    terms allow commercial use.
[ ] Real people, products and brands in the frame: we have the right to show them.

3 · VOICE
[ ] The voice is ours, a voice actor with a signed release, or an AI voice whose plan
    allows commercial use.
[ ] No clone or imitation of a real person's voice without their written permission.
[ ] A sound-alike of a famous voice counts too, even if it is "just AI".

If any box is empty, the reel does not go up.

Let your AI do the first pass: paste this prompt into Claude with the project's asset list. It flags anything without a source.

reviewer prompt · claude
You are the clearance reviewer for my AI reels. Before I post, check this reel against three risks and answer
with a table (risk · what you found · OK / FIX · how to fix):
1. Music: where does every track and sound come from? Is it licensed for commercial use on this platform?
2. Images: where does every image, logo and photo come from? Is any of it pulled from a search engine?
3. Voice: whose voice is it? Is it a clone or imitation of a real person? Is there written permission?
Here is the project: [paste the edit list, the asset folder listing, the music/voice sources].
Do not guess: if a source is unknown, mark it FIX and tell me what proof to get. This is a checklist, not legal advice.
Check 01

Music.

Trending sounds are for personal posts. Brand accounts and ads use the commercial library, licensed stock or original music.

Check 02

Images.

A search result is not a licence. Own it, license it, or generate it with a tool whose terms allow commercial use.

Check 03

Voice.

Yours, licensed, or permitted in writing. An AI copy of a real person's voice needs their permission.

03 · The facts

Every number in the reel is real.

Music · Sony Music v. Marriott

Filed in May 2024 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware over 931 alleged infringements: social media posts that used Sony songs. Sony dropped the case in October 2024; no payment is public.

Music · platform rules

The general music library on TikTok and Instagram is meant for personal use. Business accounts and ads use the commercial libraries (TikTok Commercial Sounds, Meta Sound Collection).

Images · 17 U.S.C. § 504(c)

U.S. statutory damages for copyright: $750 to $30,000 per work infringed, and up to $150,000 per work if the court finds it willful.

Voice · Tennessee ELVIS Act

In effect since July 1, 2024. It protects a person's voice, real or simulated (AI included), from commercial use without their permission.

Note: this is a checklist to avoid the obvious mistakes, not legal advice. Laws change by country and state; for a real case, talk to a lawyer.

04 · Claude session

How this reel was made.

What came back: a script checked fact by fact before the voice, a block-by-block brief, the narration with 132 time-stamped words, and two builders working at the same time: one on the hook, the payoff and the ending, the other on the three risk blocks.

The reviews that changed it: the first cut was too busy, so each moment got one hero and the data became the protagonist. Then the side-to-side sway went out, and the motion moved inside the content: numbers that count up to their value, labels that write themselves, photos that develop one by one. The cards now turn, drop with weight and land on a soft punch, never drifting sideways. The beeps were replaced by paper, pen and stamp sounds.

Music, without breaking our own rule: the "trending sound" in the music block is ours, made in code, and it cuts with a record scratch on the NOT LICENSED stamp.

What came back: 45 seconds at 1080×1920 and 30 fps, 14 Mbps, the voice plus sound effects on real events, mixed at −14 LUFS.

05 · The cut

Three risks, one check.

0:00–0:08

Don't get sued.

If you make AI reels for brands and don't want to get sued, check these three things before you post. And the last one is the one AI makes way too easy.
0:08–0:17

The music.

Trending sounds aren't licensed for ads. Sony took Marriott to court over nine hundred thirty-one posts with its songs.
0:17–0:28

The images.

In the US, one photo pulled from Google can cost up to thirty thousand dollars, and up to a hundred and fifty thousand if a court calls it willful.
0:28–0:37

The voice.

In Tennessee, using someone's voice in an ad without permission is against the law, even when it's an AI copy.
0:37–0:44

Comment SAFE.

Every reel on this page passes this check before it goes up. Comment SAFE and we'll send you our checklist.
06 · Decisions

Where the taste is.

01

The number is the hero

Each risk has one big figure that counts up while the voice says it. You understand the risk with the sound off.

02

No real logos

Sony, Marriott, Google and the platforms appear as plain names, never as logos: a reel about rights should respect them.

03

Only verified facts

No invented payouts or cases. The Sony case is shown as filed and dropped, because that is what happened.

04

Movement without sway

Cards turn, drop and land; numbers count, labels write, results load. Nothing drifts side to side.
